main_text.p: rum speculationum euoluant. Vrbicus qui-dam Romanæ Ecclesiæ consuetudinem in Sabbati ieiunio aliis Ecclesiis imponere fata-gebat. Huic respondet Augustinus, {a}varios-que errores istius Romani Vrbici refutat, nempe istos:Augustin. Epist. 86.
Ad peccatum cogi homines, quia prandetur.
Regnum Dei non esse in cibo & potu, sed in ieiunio.

Hæc Romanæ Ecclesiæ mysteria de ieiunio iam tum propalabat Romanus iste Vrbicus. Simon Petrus, inquit Romanus iste Vrbicus, Apostolorum caput, cœli ianitor, & Ecclesiæ fundamentum, extincto Simone Mago, qui fuerat Diaboli; non nisi ieiunio vincendi figura, idipsum Romanos edocuit. Hæc Augustinus irridet, & refutat, & diserte ait, Vrbicum hunc, {b}toto terrarum orbe diffusam, exceptis Romanis, & paucis adhuc Occidentalibus, blasphemare Ecclesiam. Hæc Augustinus. Ex quibus verbis constat, Ecclesiam Romanam Augustino non esse Catholicam, quia Vrbicus iste, qui Romanam collaudabat, blasphemaret Catholicam.Epist. 86.

The two final lines above are not transcribed as printed text, since the fragments do not reliably form words; they are placeholders for the cut-off columns and should be checked against a fuller scan. Printed "fpeculationum" is read as speculationum. The page number and the first letters of the running head are clear. The text "Vrbicus" in the first paragraph is read as printed.
